HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: directly examines language processing and acquisition through psychology, linguistics and neuroscience
HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

analysis: The broad plan balances literary reading, style, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, media, social identity and qualitative and historical research. The language option emphasizes language acquisition and processing, public rhetoric, social and digital discourse, AI ethics and language-model technology. Mathematical Methods supplies a required gateway for Neural Networks & Deep Learning. Public rhetoric offers direct community-engaged communication, and the introductory Dutch course supports practical use rather than advanced language analysis. The literature option adds myth, reception, adaptation, cultural institutions, museum and art-historical interpretation and documentary work. These are sustained approaches with materially different 180 EC compositions, not Dutch philology sequences. Psycholinguistics supports acquisition and processing across languages based on the actual description. General text data, media identity and historical methods are relevant complements but cannot be paired as substantive matches to Dutch corpus tools, Dutch identity, or medieval and early modern Dutch texts. Dedicated Dutch-language depth, comparative Dutch linguistics, multilingual literacy and the compulsory Dutch thesis remain gaps. The official Crossing Borders track was considered and remains represented in candidate evidence; the retained three options cover the broad and two department-level interests within the three-option maximum. UCR optional independent research is 15 EC outside the scheduled degree, distinct from Utrecht’s required 7.5 EC thesis.

alignment.rationale: Both develop close reading and literary interpretation across forms and genres.
Utrecht studies modern Dutch-language texts. UCR studies works from a range of literary traditions.
Utrecht studies early modern Dutch-language texts and culture in a dedicated course.
Utrecht studies medieval Dutch-language texts and cultures in a dedicated course.
Both study language and cognition. UCR’s Psycholinguistics focuses on acquisition and processing across languages.
Both analyze how choices in style, wording and structure shape meaning.
Utrecht examines meaning and language development specifically in Dutch. UCR studies related processes across languages.
Both study how language shapes communication. UCR approaches this through rhetoric and argument.
Both study audience, persuasion and effective communication.
Both connect reading and writing. UCR develops creative work across forms and media.
Utrecht examines Dutch grammar, structure and variation. UCR’s Dutch course develops practical introductory language skills.
Utrecht teaches corpus methods for Dutch studies and uses them to prepare students for the thesis. UCR develops general text-data skills.
Utrecht offers a dedicated comparison of Dutch languages and varieties.
Utrecht studies Dutch identity specifically. UCR examines identity and representation in a broader cultural context.
Utrecht studies multilingualism and literacy in a dedicated course.
Both develop research design and statistical analysis.
Utrecht requires a 7.5 EC thesis in Dutch after the corpus course. UCR offers optional 15 EC independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Choose 52.5 EC of electives, including a coherent 30 EC profiling package.
